# Phosphor Cam — Full Documentation

Canonical site: https://phosphor.aroy.site/
Source: https://github.com/pshycodr/phosphor-cam
Version documented: 1.4.0
License: MIT
Author: Anish Roy (Pshycodr)
Last updated: 2026-11-20

## 1. Overview

Phosphor Cam is a client-side camera and photo studio that turns a live webcam feed or a still image into stylized character, dot, block, or line art. It runs in the browser, installs as a PWA, and ships as a native Android app built from the same codebase.

The camera surface is at `/`. The photo editor, Phosphor Studio, starts at `/studio`. Both surfaces use the same five render engines, settings model, and effect pipeline, so a look tuned on the live camera can be reproduced on a photo.

Rendering happens on the device with Canvas 2D and Web Workers. Camera frames and photos are not uploaded, and the app has no account system or media upload endpoint.

## 2. Routes and surfaces

- `/` — live camera, settings, capture, and video recording.
- `/studio` — Studio empty state: file picker, drag-and-drop zone, clipboard paste, and three sample images.
- `/studio/edit` — Studio editor. This route requires a loaded image; opening it directly redirects to `/studio`. It is an application state rather than a standalone landing page.

The web app is a single-page React application. The Studio editor route is lazy-loaded so the empty Studio screen does not load the canvas worker.

## 3. Render engines

All five engines run through the same renderer interface. Character size controls the output cell size; smaller cells produce finer detail at a higher processing cost.

### ASCII

Maps each source pixel's luminance to a character from the selected character set. The character ramp runs from dark to light, and `invert` swaps the direction.

- Optional color mode draws each character in the source pixel's true RGB color.
- Monochrome mode uses the configured foreground and background colors.
- The ASCII renderer can also produce plain text at a fixed width of 150 characters for clipboard copy.

### Dither

Uses Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion. Each pixel is quantized to the nearest available output value, and the quantization error is distributed to neighboring pixels with the standard 7/16, 3/16, 5/16, 1/16 weights.

- Monochrome mode dithers luminance and maps the result to the foreground/background palette.
- Color mode dithers the red, green, and blue channels independently and draws the resulting RGB values.
- Output is upscaled with nearest-neighbor sampling for crisp blocks.

### Halftone

Recreates the image as a grid of dots whose size encodes brightness, similar to a printed halftone screen.

- Brightness is mapped to one of 64 dot levels; level 0 draws no dot.
- Odd rows are shifted by half a cell to form a brick pattern and break up vertical seams.
- Monochrome mode tints the dot atlas with the foreground color.
- Color mode draws the dots as an alpha mask and paints the source frame through it, preserving per-dot color.
- `invert` swaps the dot mapping and the foreground/background colors for a true negative.

### Voxel

Quantizes the image into solid color blocks.

- Flat mode draws one block per cell with a single ImageData blit and nearest-neighbor upscale.
- 3D mode draws raised cubes with top, right, and bottom faces from a pre-rendered sprite atlas.
- Monochrome mode builds a 16-step color ramp between the background and foreground colors.
- Color mode uses a fixed 22-color palette.
- A 4×4 Bayer ordered-dither offset is applied before palette lookup to reduce banding.
- `invert` inverts the RGB channels before palette lookup, producing a full negative.

### Lines

Renders each row or column as one continuous ribbon whose thickness follows source luminance.

- `lineDirection` selects horizontal or vertical ribbons.
- Edges are Catmull-Rom splines converted to Bézier curves, so the ribbon flows instead of stepping between samples.
- Monochrome mode fills the ribbon with the foreground color.
- Color mode paints each cell with its true source RGB.
- Minimum and maximum ribbon thickness are derived from the cell size.

## 4. ASCII character sets

There are 22 character sets. The leading space in most sets represents the darkest level.

```text
standard        " .:-=+*#%@MB"
simple          " .+#@"
blocks          " ░▒▓█"
matrix          " 01"
edges           "  .,-_~:;=!*#$@"
dense           " .`^",:;Il!i~+_-?][}{1)(|\/tfjrxnuvczXYUJCLQ0OZmwqpdbkhao*#MW&8%B@$"
lines           " ─│┌┐└┘├┤┬┴┼"
heavyLines      " ═║╔╗╚╝╠╣╦╩╬"
invertedBlocks  " █▓▒░ "
braille         " ⠁⠃⠇⡇⣇⣧⣷⣿"
dots            " .•◦●◉"
circles         " .oO◌◎●"
spark           " .`'^*✦✧✶✹"
tech            " .:+=xX$#"
digital         " .:-=+*#%@"
alphabetic      " .abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
upperAlpha      " .ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
numeric         " 0123456789"
mixed           " .:-=+*#%@abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
arrows          " .<>^v"
binaryDense     " 01#@"
runic           " .ᚠᚢᚦᚨᚱᚲᚷᚹ"
```

## 5. Adjustments and appearance

- Character size: 2–30 px.
- Contrast: 0.5×–3.0×.
- Brightness: −100 to +100.
- Color mode: draws source colors instead of a fixed palette.
- Invert: swaps light and dark handling.
- Foreground and background: any hex color.
- Color controls: H/S/B sliders, hex input, six presets, random foreground/background, and a foreground/background swap.
- Six color presets: Matrix (`#00ff00` on `#000000`), Amber (`#ffb000` on `#000000`), Cyan (`#00e5ff` on `#000000`), Paper (`#1a1a1a` on `#f5f5f0`), Neon Pink (`#ff2e88` on `#0a0014`), and Blood (`#ff1a1a` on `#0a0000`).
- Voxel 3D mode: toggles flat blocks versus raised cubes.
- Line direction: horizontal or vertical.
- On phones, the camera frame can be set to 1:1, 3:4, or full screen. The default is 3:4. Desktop uses the available stage.

Default settings are ASCII mode, the standard character set, 10 px characters, 1.2× contrast, 0 brightness, green (`#00ff00`) on black (`#000000`), 3D voxels enabled, 4× capture scale, 3:4 aspect ratio, horizontal lines, all effects off, and PNG capture.

## 6. Effects

Seven optional passes are available. Each has an on/off state and an intensity value. Effects apply to the live preview, saved images, and exports.

The pipeline runs in this order:

1. Chromatic aberration
2. Glow
3. Bloom
4. Halation
5. Vignette
6. Scanlines
7. Grain

Behavior:

- **Chromatic aberration** splits the red, green, and blue channels horizontally by up to 8 px at full intensity.
- **Glow** adds a small, soft additive blur with a slight brightness lift.
- **Bloom** adds a wider, brighter additive blur with increased contrast for highlight bleed.
- **Halation** adds a wide, warm orange blur around highlights, simulating film halation.
- **Vignette** darkens the frame radially from the middle toward the corners.
- **Scanlines** overlays a repeating 3 px dark line pattern.
- **Grain** overlays animated 128 px noise tiles with an overlay blend.

## 7. Phosphor Studio

Studio is the photo-editing side of the app. Open it from the Studio button in the camera header or directly at `/studio`.

### Loading images

- Select an image with the file picker.
- Drop an image onto the viewport.
- Paste an image with the Paste button or `Ctrl`/`Cmd` + `V`.
- Choose one of three built-in samples: Clock Tower, Flower, or People sitting.

Studio currently edits images only. Video files show a “Video editing is coming soon” message.

Uploaded images are downscaled before editing to at most 1,600 px on the long edge and to roughly the viewport's pixel budget, with a 640×480 floor. Previews and exports then process the same bounded source.

### Presets

There are ten presets in three categories.

| Preset | Category | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phosphor CRT | Retro CRT | Green ASCII terminal look with standard characters, glow, vignette, and scanlines. |
| Amber Terminal | Retro CRT | Warm amber ASCII look with bloom, halation, vignette, scanlines, and grain. |
| Matrix Rain | Retro CRT | High-contrast green ASCII using the `matrix` (`0`/`1`) set, with glow, chromatic aberration, vignette, scanlines, and grain. |
| Cyberpunk 2077 | Print & Dither | Color dither with a neon magenta accent, glow, chromatic aberration, vignette, scanlines, and grain. |
| Newspaper Print | Print & Dither | Monochrome Floyd–Steinberg dither with dark ink on off-white paper, vignette, and grain. |
| Cyan Halftone | Print & Dither | Cyan halftone dots on a deep blue-black background with glow and vignette. |
| Pop Art Halftone | Print & Dither | Full-color halftone dots with halation, vignette, and grain. |
| Broadcast Lines | Digital & 3D | Horizontal luminance ribbons in teal on near-black, with chromatic aberration, vignette, and scanlines. |
| Architectural Blueprint | Digital & 3D | Vertical white line hatching on blueprint blue, with vignette and grain. |
| 8-Bit Voxels | Digital & 3D | Color 3D voxel cubes at 12 px with vignette. |

### Editing

- The inspector is a 344 px right rail on desktop and a persistent bottom sheet below 1024 px.
- Zoom ranges from 0.5× to 4×. Mouse wheel and pinch zoom; double-click toggles 2× and reset; pan when zoomed in.
- Hold the Compare button to crossfade to the original photo.
- Undo and redo cover adjustments, presets, and color changes. History holds up to 30 entries.
- Reset restores the default settings.
- Keyboard shortcuts: `Ctrl`/`Cmd` + `Z` undo, `Ctrl`/`Cmd` + `Shift` + `Z` or `Ctrl` + `Y` redo, `Esc` closes the export dialog.
- On touch screens, a horizontal swipe at 1× zoom steps through the render engines.
- Leaving the editor with unsaved changes opens a discard confirmation. Android back follows the same flow.

### Export

- Formats: PNG, JPEG, and WEBP.
- Scale: 1×–20×. Above 12× the interface warns that large canvases may take longer or fail.
- Save image downloads the render.
- Copy image copies a PNG render to the clipboard.
- Copy ASCII is available when the ASCII renderer is active and copies plain text.

## 8. Camera

- Requests video-only camera access with an ideal resolution of 1920×1080; audio is not requested.
- Front and back camera switching. The front-camera preview is mirrored.
- The viewfinder center-crops the stream to the selected aspect ratio; the crop is mirrored after cropping, so people and objects keep their shape.
- Every renderer, photo capture, recording, and copied ASCII sample uses the same cropped canvas, so the saved result matches the preview.
- The frame size follows the viewfinder stage; the live FPS, render time, and frame size are displayed in the header.
- Photo capture uses the active renderer's high-resolution capture path.
- Video recording captures the rendered canvas with `MediaRecorder` at 30 fps and 2.5 Mbps. It prefers VP9 WebM, then VP8 WebM, H.264 MP4, WebM, and MP4.
- Copy ASCII is available only for the ASCII renderer.
- Settings open as a 360 px right rail on desktop and a bottom drawer on phones. `Esc` closes the desktop rail.
- Phone gestures: horizontal swipe steps the renderer, upward swipe opens settings, downward swipe closes them, pinch steps the aspect ratio, and double-tap flips the camera. Renderer, pinch, and flip gestures are disabled while recording or while the settings editor is open.

## 9. Capture, recording, and export

- Camera snapshot: uses the active renderer's capture path and the configured capture scale for ASCII, Dither, Halftone, and Voxel. Lines uses a fixed 4× capture scale.
- Camera recording: records the rendered canvas, not the raw camera stream, so effects and the selected engine are included.
- Studio export: renders the bounded source image at the selected format and scale.
- Clipboard: rendered images can be copied in Studio; ASCII text can be copied in both the camera and Studio.
- Capture scale: 1×–20×, with a warning above 12×.

## 10. Performance and architecture

- Rendering runs in a Web Worker using Canvas 2D and OffscreenCanvas, keeping the interface responsive while frames are processed.
- The camera pipeline targets 60 FPS; actual FPS depends on the device, renderer, character size, effects, and frame size.
- Settings are shared between the camera and Studio through a Zustand store. The Studio editor has its own history stack.
- The Studio editor route is lazy-loaded, so the empty Studio screen does not ship the canvas worker.
- The PWA registers a service worker in production. Navigation uses network-first caching; other assets use stale-while-revalidate. The Android build is fully offline after install.

## 11. Privacy and security

- Camera frames, photos, and renders are processed locally and are not uploaded.
- There is no account system, cloud sync, or server-side media processing.
- Camera access requires a secure context: HTTPS or `localhost`.
- The project does not publish a dedicated security email. The repository issue tracker is the only published contact channel.

## 12. Browser support

Requires `getUserMedia`, Canvas 2D, and ES2020+.

| Browser | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome | 90+ |
| Firefox | 88+ |
| Safari | 14+ |
| Edge | 90+ |

The interface is responsive down to 360 px wide. Touch targets are at least 44 px on mobile, and reduced-motion and reduced-transparency preferences are respected.

## 13. PWA and Android

- The web app is installable as a PWA with a standalone display, a dark theme (`#080908`), and 192 px and 512 px icons.
- The Android build uses Capacitor with application ID `site.aroy.phosphor` and is built from the same source.
- Android releases are signed and published automatically. The app works offline after install.
- On Android, saved images and videos are written to `Documents/Phosphor-cam/images` and `Documents/Phosphor-cam/videos`.
- The Android app handles the system back gesture, including the Studio discard flow and exit hint.

## 14. Technology stack

At version 1.4.0:

- React 19.2.5 and React DOM 19.2.5
- TypeScript 6.0
- Vite 8
- Tailwind CSS 4.2
- Zustand 5
- React Router 8
- Capacitor 8
- Vaul 1.1
- Lucide React and React Icons
- react-hot-toast
- Canvas 2D, Web Workers, OffscreenCanvas
- MediaStream API and MediaRecorder
- Bun 1.4.0 for development and builds

The app is a static Vite build deployed to Cloudflare Pages. There is no application server.

## 15. Limitations and roadmap

- Studio supports images only. Video editing is planned for a later release.
- Camera access requires permission and a secure context.
- Large capture scales above 12× may be slow or fail on devices with limited canvas memory.
- Lines captures at a fixed 4× scale rather than the configurable 1×–20× scale.
- Browser support is limited to browsers with `getUserMedia`, Canvas 2D, and ES2020+.
- There is no account, cloud storage, or cross-device sync.
